A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All pages, including appendices, equations and six figures, are readable and support comparison; no material gaps were identified.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on discretized Gaussian mixtures and binarized MNIST, including reward, distributional distance, diversity, generated samples and ESS traces.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including the appendix experiments using ReMDM and UDLM.

M1.justification: The twisted SMC sampler, Taylor-approximated proposal, Gumbel-Softmax relaxation and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. New Appendix B derives connections to continuous-time SMC without introducing a distinct proposed sampling procedure. Equation (18)'s changed factor symbol is a notation correction.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Gaussian-mixture scenarios and binarized MNIST digit conditioning. The ReMDM and UDLM experiments already appear in v1's appendix; no continuous-time experiment or additional task is introduced.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators: the locally optimal oracle proposal for Gaussian mixtures, reverse-process-proposal SMC and approximate guidance. Newly cited SMC methods are discussed but not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 4 and the experimental appendices retain the architectures, rewards, metrics, 100 sampling steps, particle counts, noise and tempering schedules, ESS thresholds and resampling procedures. The continuous-time discussion introduces no experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The proposal comparisons through reward and ESS traces, and the MNIST analyses examining remasking and persistent guidance, are retained unchanged. Figure 3's relocation does not add an analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed lists, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Reward averaging and ESS reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 1–6 retain identical values, traces and sample grids. For example, Figure 2's rewards remain -2.82 for reverse-process SMC, -0.00 for first-order-proposal SMC and -0.52 for approximate guidance. No result entries or findings are added.

T1.justification: New Appendix B adds CTMC rate definitions and constraints, Kolmogorov equations, and continuous-time importance-weight derivations connecting SMC formulations. This substantially expands the formal content; the existing gradient analysis is retained and renumbered. The new derivation contains sign and rate-index inconsistencies, including Equation (29) and the final logarithmic rate terms.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free, asymptotically unbiased reward alignment through an approximate locally optimal proposal, supported by synthetic and image experiments. The appendix addition does not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: V2 removes v1's statement listing continuous-time extension as future work and supplies a mathematical connection in Appendix B. Existing interpretations of diversity loss and masked-token irreversibility, and limitations concerning complex tasks, comparator coverage and hand-crafted tempering, remain.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain the same, including MLP/U-Net descriptions, reward estimation, resampling settings and the ReMDM cap of 0.1. Both versions retain the same statement promising future code availability; no additional implementation or resource information is supplied.

R1.justification: Appendix B substantially expands the relationship to prior SMC research through mathematical connections with Ou, Holderrieth and Lee. Related work also adds Singhal, Skreta and He, alongside new CTMC background references. Campbell and Sun are removed with the continuous-time future-work sentence.

P1.justification: V2 inserts Appendix B, populates the previously empty Contents section and renumbers subsequent appendices. Existing prose receives limited editing, including a shorter background sentence and workshop acceptance text. The running title is replaced by the template text 'Submission and Formatting Instructions for ICML 2025'.

P2.justification: All six figure graphics, axes and legends are retained. Figure 2 switches columns, Figure 3 moves to a separate page, and Algorithm 1 is repositioned amid the expanded appendix. The contents list and text reflow alter layout without a visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The contents list and expanded research connections help, but v2's principal scientific addition introduces correctness problems. Equation (29) has the wrong integral sign even for a path without jumps, and Appendix B.2's final expression logs a diagonal CTMC rate, which Equation (24) makes nonpositive. With the original sampler and empirical evidence unchanged, these added problems outweigh the limited explanatory and navigation gains.
